_note: Secrets: what the public doesn't know about you, and might one day. 'size' (0.5-3) sets how hard it hits when it leaks. PAST: the leader's small skeletons from the years as mayor (one or two drawn at founding; never anything big). PARTY: what a hastily hired politician may bring with them. HYPOCRISY: grows each time your words contradict your record (see sim.gd). Money secrets come from the secret offers in content.json and use their leak events' titles and texts. RESPONSES: what you do when one leaks (the chosen wording matters: each has lines with tones; 'gaffe' marks a line that is simply wrong). Placeholders: {leader} {party} {home} {name} {source} {figure}. Drafts: rewrite freely.

PAST.title: {leader}'s old contract for a friend
PAST.what: As mayor, you gave the {home} bus-shelter contract to an old school friend's firm. It was cheap and they were good. It was also not put out to tender.
PAST.text: Documents show {leader}, as mayor of {home}, handed a city contract to a friend's firm without a tender.

PAST.title: A cousin on the {home} payroll
PAST.what: Your cousin spent two years as a 'cultural adviser' to the city of {home}. Nobody is quite sure what was advised.
PAST.text: {leader}'s cousin drew a city salary in {home} as a 'cultural adviser'. Former staff say they never saw the advice.

PAST.title: The {home} tram budget
PAST.what: The tram line in {home} cost twice the budget, and you signed the second half without telling the council.
PAST.text: Council papers show {leader} doubled the {home} tram budget without a council vote.

PAST.title: {leader}'s city flat
PAST.what: For a year as mayor you lived in a city-owned flat at a quarter of the market rent. It was legal. It does not look it.
PAST.text: {leader} rented a city-owned flat in {home} at a quarter of the market rate while mayor.

PAST.title: {leader}'s old speech
PAST.what: Ten years ago, at a private dinner, you said things about the voters of your own region you would rather nobody had recorded. Somebody did.
PAST.text: A recording from a private dinner has {leader} calling ordinary voters 'easily led'.

PARTY.title: {name}'s unpaid taxes
PARTY.text: {name}, newly promoted in {party}, owes the tax office three years of returns.

PARTY.title: {name}'s old posts
PARTY.text: {name}, one of {party}'s new faces, spent years posting things online the party would rather not see printed.

PARTY.title: {name}'s failed company
PARTY.text: {name}'s last company went bankrupt owing its workers two months' wages. {name} now speaks for {party}.

elites.title: {leader} attacks the elites, banks their money
elites.what: You speak against the people at the top, and your party takes business money. Every speech makes the gap wider.
elites.text: {leader} has spent the year attacking 'the people at the top'. {party}'s accounts show the people at the top paying for it.

workers.title: The workers' champion and the chamber of commerce
workers.what: You speak for workers against business, and the Chamber of Commerce helps pay your bills.
workers.text: {party} talks like a union and is funded like a bank, the papers say, with the receipts.

LIE.title: The denial falls apart
LIE.text: Your denial lasted until {source} printed the proof. Now the story is not what you did; it is that you lied about it.

EVIDENCE.carlos: Boss, they have the papers. Denying this is a long shot.
They have someone talking, boss, but no papers. Could go either way.
It's a rumour, boss. One source, no paper. We could make it go away.

deny.label: Deny it
deny.help: Free if it holds. If they have proof, a worse story follows.

lines.text: There is no truth in this, and our lawyers are looking at it.
A lie, from start to finish, and everyone knows who's spreading it!

own.label: Own it and apologise
own.help: Costs now, ends it. Honest outlets and older voters respect it.

lines.text: I got this wrong. I'm sorry, and I'm putting it right.
I made a mistake. Most people have. The difference is mine was in the newspaper.

attack.label: Attack the messenger
attack.help: Your own people rally; honest outlets turn on you. Works best when nobody trusts anyone.

lines.text: Of course they printed this. Look who owns them, and look who's rising in the polls.
They are frightened of us, and this is what frightened people do.

subject.label: Change the subject
subject.help: Start a louder argument elsewhere. Uses one of this month's actions.

lines.text: People don't care about this. They care about the price of bread, and so do I.
While they dig through old papers, the country is falling apart. Let's talk about that.

scapegoat.label: Ask {figure} to take the fall
scapegoat.help: {figure} resigns 'for personal reasons' and the story dies with the job. It has a price, and a deal like that is a secret too.

lines.text: {figure} has resigned. I accept the decision, and I thank {figure} for the work.
{figure} did the decent thing. That's more than you can say for most people in this business.

money.text: Money is money. Everyone takes it; we're just honest enough to spend it on something.
